text: 其实很大一部分男生，
en: Actually, a great many of the lads,

text: 不是只看脸蛋好不好看的，
en: don't only care whether you have a pretty face,

text: 也在乎你的身高，
en: but also care about your height,

text: 也在乎你的学历的，
en: also care about your academic qualifications,

text: 也在乎你的家境，
en: also care about your family background,

text: 也在乎你的工作，
en: also care about your job,

text: 也在乎你的收入和前途，
en: also care about your income and prospects,

text: 也在乎你的兴趣爱好是否广泛，
en: also care about whether your interests and hobbies are wide-ranging,

text: 所有女生在乎的东西，
en: Everything that girls care about,

text: 反过来放在他们身上，同样适用，
en: applies to them just as much in reverse,

text: 所以，不要被一些营销号洗脑了，
en: so, don't let those marketing accounts brainwash you,

text: 以为所有男生们就只看脸。
en: thinking that all lads only care about looks.

text: 他似乎读过很多书。
en: He seems to have read a good many books.

text: 他各方面知道蛮多的。
en: He knows quite a bit about all sorts of things.

text: 他平时穿着都干干净净的。
en: He always keeps himself neatly dressed.

text: 他篮球似乎打得挺好的。
en: He seems to play basketball rather well.

text: 他好像十分喜欢打游戏。
en: He seems to quite like playing video games.

text: 他看上去学习还可以。
en: He looks like he does alright at his studies.

text: 他谈吐还是挺有修养的。
en: His manner of speaking still shows a fair bit of refinement.

text: 他整天笑嘻嘻的。
en: He's always smiling cheerfully.

text: 他好像对我没有兴趣。
en: He doesn't seem to be interested in me.

text: 他也许早就有女朋友。
en: He probably already has a girlfriend.

text: 他曾经是读过一些书，各种各样，如今印象最深的却是其中一些荤段儿。
en: He did once read a fair few books of all kinds, yet what strikes him most deeply now is some of the bawdy jokes among them.

text: 他闲来无事会了解了解各方面的知识，只求略懂一二，来日好装逼。
en: When he has nothing much to do he'll pick up a bit of knowledge about all sorts of subjects, happy with just a superficial grasp, so he can show off some day.

text: 相比人前一本正经的穿搭，他更喜欢夹拖沙滩裤的自由。
en: Compared with a proper, buttoned-up outfit in front of others, he prefers the freedom of flip-flops and beach shorts.

text: 在野球场不知被虐过多少回，他打球只是图个开心，锻炼锻炼身体。
en: Having been thrashed on the pickup court who knows how many times, he only plays for a bit of fun, to get some exercise.

text: 如果有什么不让业余生活那么无聊，他也不会想去打游戏。
en: If there were something to keep his leisure time from being so boring, he wouldn't feel like playing video games either.

text: 要不是怕挂科，鬼才去学习。
en: If it weren't for the fear of failing his exams, he'd be damned if he studied.

text: 还是和死党们聊天舒服啊，想怎么骂娘吐槽就怎么说。
en: It's still most comfortable chatting with his mates — you can swear and grumble to your heart's content.

text: 他想。
en: He thought.

text: 他至今都不让那几个朋友向外透露他喝醉了抱着别人腿哭的场面。
en: To this day he hasn't let those few friends let slip the time he got drunk, hugged someone's leg and cried.

text: 他早就注意到你了。
en: He noticed you long ago.

text: 他怕你接受不了这样的他。
en: He's afraid you won't be able to accept this side of him.

text: 我观察了一下我家三代男人，得出的结论是：熊孩子！
en: I took a look at the men in my family across three generations and concluded: naughty children!

text: 真的，你甭管他们在外面有多成熟稳重风光无限，在家就是个彻头彻尾的熊孩子。
en: Honestly, no matter how mature, steady and successful they seem outside, at home they're utter naughty children.

text: 我姥爷，老式知识分子，离休老干部，19岁创办第一所学校，去世后教育局给他立了塑像，你可以想象他平时在外面的样子。
en: My grandfather, an old-style intellectual and a retired veteran cadre, founded his first school at nineteen, and after he passed away the education bureau erected a statue of him; you can imagine what he's usually like out in the world.

text: 在家，他就是个完全依赖我姥姥的小孩，用他的话说，是"这辈子没往自己家墙上钉过一颗钉子"。
en: At home he's a child who depends entirely on my grandmother, and in his own words, "I've never hammered a single nail into the wall of my own home."

text: 家里什么东西在哪都不知道，一天能叫我姥姥名字八百遍。
en: He hasn't a clue where anything in the house is, and will call my grandmother's name eight hundred times a day.

text: 以前楼下有个仓房，经常有小偷光顾。
en: There used to be a storeroom downstairs that thieves would often visit.

text: 姥爷想半天，把仓房清空，门也不锁了，门外贴上"请进"，门里贴着"慢走"，随便小偷来去。
en: My grandfather thought for ages, emptied the storeroom, left the door unlocked, stuck a "Please come in" on the outside and a "Take your time" on the inside, letting thieves come and go as they pleased.

text: 后来发现东西是不丢了，总是会多很多垃圾，于是干脆指挥儿子把门钉死，大有"我不用你也别用"的架势。
en: Later he found that things did stop going missing, but there was always far more rubbish, so he simply ordered his son to nail the door shut, in a manner that said, "If I can't use it, neither can you."

text: 姥姥恨得牙痒痒，姥爷得意洋洋。
en: My grandmother itched with rage, while my grandfather was triumphant.

text: 极度挑食，就爱吃豆腐，姥姥就天天顿顿给他做豆腐。
en: He's extremely fussy about food, only wanting to eat tofu, so my grandmother made him tofu for every single meal.

text: 好商量歹商量早饭不吃豆腐了，吵着要吃豆腐乳…
en: After much haggling he agreed to skip tofu at breakfast, then kicked up a fuss to eat fermented tofu…

text: 后来就得了痛风…
en: Later he developed gout…

text: 姥姥不让他再吃豆腐，于是姥爷每顿一言不发默默吃饭，然后回书房赋诗一首表达悲愤心情，必须趁姥姥不注意的时候把诗贴在厨房门口。
en: My grandmother forbade him from eating tofu again, so at every meal my grandfather would eat in silence, then go back to his study and compose a poem expressing his sorrow and indignation — he had to stick the poem on the kitchen door when my grandmother wasn't looking.

text: 怕姥姥看不懂，还要加上注音和注释。
en: Fearing my grandmother wouldn't understand, he even added phonetic notation and annotations.

text: 你能想象一个人写首诗，自己在上面标注①②，下面写这个词的具体解释吗？
en: Can you imagine someone writing a poem and marking ①② on it himself, then writing the specific explanation of the word below?

text: 我爸爸，77级本科生，十几年前就年入百万的事业有成的理工科男人。
en: My father, an undergraduate of the class of 1977, a successful man of science and engineering who was already earning a million a year more than ten years ago.

text: 理智，稳重，顾家，都是他的标签，在家也是把我妈宠得无法无天。
en: Rational, steady and family-minded — all his labels — and at home he spoils my mother rotten too.

text: 但是，但凡做了什么得意事，必须跑到我妈面前显摆，一副"表扬我表扬我快点表扬我"的表情。
en: But whenever he does something worth boasting about, he must run to my mother to show off, with a look that says, "Praise me, praise me, praise me quickly."

text: 还志得意满地自问自答"什么是爸？
en: He would also, full of himself, ask and answer his own question, "What is a dad?

text: 这就是爸。
en: That is a dad.

text: "大概是开了"叫爸爸"的先河。
en: "He probably started the whole "call me daddy" trend.

text: 好奇心太强，只要是买回来的没见过的电器和机械，总想拆开看看，又大概率安装不回去。
en: His curiosity is too strong; any new electrical appliance or machine bought home that he hasn't seen before, he always wants to take apart, and more often than not can't put it back together.

text: 后来我妈每次买新奇的东西都买两个，我爸玩坏一个，再拿出另一个用。
en: Later my mother would buy two of anything novel she bought, so my father could break one playing with it and she'd bring out the other to use.

text: 生气的时候不讲道理，也控制不住脾气。
en: When angry he's unreasonable and can't control his temper.

text: 他发脾气不是打人毁物也不是爆粗口，而是摆出一副雄辩的架势要跟你"讲道理"。
en: His outbursts aren't about hitting people or smashing things, nor about swearing; rather, he puts on the air of a great debater and wants to "reason" with you.

text: 当然道理里不乏文字游戏强词夺理和诡辩。
en: Of course, his reasoning is full of wordplay, sophistry and specious arguments.

text: 年轻时我妈还跟他吵吵架，后来干脆不理他，把他发脾气的声音当背景音，反正等他脾气过去，就会臊眉耷眼地过来道歉。
en: When young my mother would still argue with him, but later she simply ignored him, treating the sound of his tantrums as background noise; after all, once his temper passed, he'd come over sheepishly to apologise.

text: 我老公，外人眼中的阳光暖男，成熟体贴，才华横溢。
en: My husband, in others' eyes a sunny, warm-hearted bloke, mature, considerate and brilliant.

text: 在家，哈！
en: At home, ha!

text: 热爱熬夜，也不知为什么，反正就想等等再睡。
en: He loves staying up late, and though no one knows why, he just wants to wait a bit longer before sleeping.

text: 等什么呢？
en: Wait for what?

text: 也不知道，反正就想等等。
en: No one knows either; he just wants to wait a bit.

text: 每次我都等到困得死去活来，忍无可忍地拉他睡觉。
en: Every time I wait until I'm absolutely knackered, then haul him off to bed when I can't take it any more.

text: 他的逃睡三板斧：抽烟，上厕所，检查门窗。
en: His three sleep-dodging tricks: smoking, going to the loo, checking the doors and windows.

text: 什么时候说睡觉，什么时候要便便，要是一晚上不睡就一晚上也想不起这茬，做这三件事就能磨蹭一个多小时。
en: The moment you say it's time to sleep, he needs a poo; if he stays up the whole night he won't think of it once, but doing these three things lets him dawdle for over an hour.

text: 有时候他明明已经很困了，都揉眼睛了，也叫嚣着不睡。
en: Sometimes he's clearly already knackered, rubbing his eyes, yet still clamouring that he won't sleep.

text: 摁到床上，还嚷嚷着"不要睡，要打滚，猫儿，你看我倒立"。
en: Pinned onto the bed, he still yells, "Don't sleep, I want to roll around, kitty, look, I'm doing a handstand!"

text: 只要安静三分钟，呼噜就响起来了，而这时候我因为和他斗智斗勇来着，斗志正盛反而睡不着。
en: If you keep him quiet for three minutes, the snores start up, but by then, having been locked in a battle of wits with him, my fighting spirit is so high I can't get to sleep instead.

text: 每到此时我都真是银牙咬碎，恨不得把他摇起来狠狠揍一顿。
en: Every time this happens I truly grit my teeth, wishing I could shake him awake and give him a good thrashing.

text: 有天晚上，我先睡了没管他，睡到两点多突然惊醒，发现身边没有人，赶紧出去看看。
en: One night I fell asleep first and left him be; I woke with a start past two in the morning and found no one beside me, so hurried out to look.

text: 下楼一看，这货正坐在厨房地上，教我家猫玩"三仙归洞"（三个碗一个球，让猫猜球在哪个碗里），猫已经输给他一堆小鱼干了。
en: I went downstairs and there he was, sitting on the kitchen floor, teaching our cat to play "Three Immortals Return to the Cave" (three bowls and one ball, getting the cat to guess which bowl the ball is in), and the cat had already lost him a pile of dried fish.

text: 所以，我真的深信，男孩子的内心永远不会长大。
en: So I really do believe it: a boy's heart never grows up.

text: 他们在外面再成熟再成功，在心爱的人面前都还是个孩子，不，熊孩子。
en: No matter how mature or successful they are outside, in front of the one they love they're still a child — no, a naughty child.

text: 谢谢大家喜欢，突然这么多赞，哈哈哈
en: Thanks everyone for the love, suddenly so many likes, hahaha

text: 那些没听长辈劝告，与穷男朋友结婚的人现在都过得咋样了？
en: Those who didn't heed their elders' advice and married a poor boyfriend — how are they doing now?

text: 国庆节的时候和男朋友去香港迪士尼，他好像兴致缺缺。
en: On National Day I went to Hong Kong Disneyland with my boyfriend, and he seemed rather unenthusiastic.

text: 逛到美国小镇大街的纪念品店的时候，他一个180cm+的大老爷们对着蜘蛛侠的纪念水杯发出了少女般的尖叫：“我要这个！
en: When we got to the souvenir shop on Main Street, U.S.A., this 180cm-plus grown man let out a girlish scream at a Spider-Man souvenir cup: “I want this!”

text: 啊我好喜欢蜘蛛侠！
en: Ah, I love Spider-Man so much!

text: 上面这个贴着的英文标签是啥？
en: What does this English label stuck on top say?

text: 你给我翻译翻译！
en: Translate it for me!

text: 我看了下和他说：“这上面说加了热水蜘蛛侠眼睛会变色”
en: I looked and said to him: “It says here that if you add hot water, Spider-Man's eyes change colour.”

text: “啊啊啊啊眼睛变色？
en: “Ah ah ah, the eyes change colour?

text: 我要买！
en: I want to buy it!

text: ”然后他抓着他心爱的蜘蛛侠跑去结账了…
en: ”Then he grabbed his beloved Spider-Man and ran off to the checkout…

text: emmm…
en: emmm…

text: 据说他把水杯带去公司用，跟献宝似的在公司里转了一圈，逢人就往杯子里倒热水展示蜘蛛侠变色的眼睛…
en: Apparently he took the cup to work and paraded it around the office like a prized treasure, pouring hot water into it for everyone to show off Spider-Man's colour-changing eyes…

text: 所以说，男生的心里可能永远住着一个小男孩吧，无论他年纪多大，无论他身高多高，无论他社会地位社会地位是什么样，他心里还是永远住着一个小男孩。
en: So, perhaps a boy always has a little boy living in his heart, no matter how old he is, no matter how tall he is, no matter what his social standing is — there's always a little boy living in his heart.

text: 更新一下：
en: Update:

text: 加开水之前，蜘蛛侠boy的眼睛是眯眯眼～
en: Before adding boiling water, Spider-Man boy's eyes are all squinty～

text: 加开水之后，他的眼睛睁开了！
en: After adding boiling water, his eyes open up!

text: 如果你加开水，蜘蛛侠的眼睛会全部变成白色！
en: If you add boiling water, Spider-Man's eyes turn completely white!

text: 就问你酷不酷！
en: Just tell me, isn't that cool!

text: 炫不炫！
en: Isn't it brilliant!

text: 试问：有哪一个26岁的大老爷们不想拥有一个这样的水杯呢？
en: I ask you: what 26-year-old grown man wouldn't want a cup like this?

text: 我跟你们说，那个杯盖，也是他自己选的…
en: Let me tell you, that cup lid — he chose it himself…

text: 这呼之欲出的少女心…
en: This girlishness, all but bursting out…

text: 蜘蛛侠要是知道自己头上顶个小熊，不知道会不会开心…
en: If Spider-Man knew a little bear was perched on his head, I wonder whether he'd be pleased…

text: 杯子是2017年10月在香港迪士尼买的，如果各位知友想买的话可以自己去迪士尼买哟！
en: The cup was bought at Hong Kong Disneyland in October 2017; if any fellow Zhihu users want to buy one, you can go to Disneyland yourselves!

text: 这真的不是个广告贴，毕竟迪士尼有必要找我给他们做广告吗…
en: This really isn't an advertorial — after all, why would Disney need to ask me to advertise for them…
